issues.what: The explanation given for r0_f1's control percentile (100.0) disagreeing with its pooled diff (-848) is wrong in direction. FINDINGS says 'the 57 skipped rows sit in sessions whose other units are better still'. Recomputed: within the 54 sessions where r0_f1 fires, the kept units average -520 INR and the skipped +32, i.e. the other units are worse. The real mechanism is that 21 of the 57 skipped units are the only unit of their session (the rule skips the whole session); they net +98,329 INR (mean +4,682) and are invisible to the session-matched random control and to harness.spa's selection gain (nothing kept -> nothing drawn, gain = 0). On the control-visible rows (36 skipped units in 33 partially-skipped sessions) the diff is +1,864 (kept > skipped in 23 of 33 sessions), which is why control pct = 100 and the 5-min studentised SPA p = 0.045. The same blindness applies to r0_f2 (10 all-skipped sessions, 12 units, +48,273). The verdict (r0_f1 fails go/no-go, SPA p not evidence for the family) is unaffected, but the stated reason, reused as 'the same effect as in h1_gate_audit and session_stop', is incorrect.
issues.evidence: Recomputed from OUT/data/5minute L1 IS rows with the study's own mask semantics: fired sessions 54; all-units-skipped sessions 21 holding 21 units, skipped net sum 98,329; partially-skipped sessions 33 holding 36 units, mean -2,680; kept mean in fired sessions -520 vs skipped +32; pooled diff on control-visible rows +1,864 vs full pooled diff -848; harness.selection_gain sum +43,340 over 387 active sessions.
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with the mechanism: the session-matched control and the SPA selection gain cannot see sessions in which the gate keeps nothing, so a sparse rule that skips whole (single-unit) sessions can score control 100 while its pooled diff is negative; report the share of skipped units in all-skipped sessions (21 of 57 for r0_f1, 12 of 55 for r0_f2) next to the control percentile, and state it as a known limitation of the control for sparse rules rather than as 'session composition'.

issues.what: The stated Holm rule for untestable rules does not match the code. FINDINGS (script docstring, section 6) says 'an untestable rule enters with p = 1', but score_round0.py enters the ledger's perm_p whenever it is not None: r0_m6 enters with 0.5752 and r0_f8 with 0.3633 (both computed on a single skipped unit); only r0_m8 (perm_p None) enters with 1. No effect on the result: min raw p 0.0625 x 16 = 1.0, so every Holm-adjusted p is 1.0 either way.

issues.fix: Either force p = 1 for rules with skipped_n <= 1 (untestable flag) before Holm, or reword the definition to 'a rule with no skipped unit enters with p = 1; a one-unit rule enters with its (meaningless) perm_p'.

issues.what: The one-paragraph result and the REPORT.md wording generalise from the 16 specific rules to the user's observations ('the user's cells are not where the losers are'; 'the user's four observations, written blind in config form ... do not mark losing Foundation SETUPs'). The evidence supports only that these 16 operationalisations do not: 3 of 16 are untestable through an admitted unit error, r0_m6/r0_f6 and r0_m4/r0_f4 each carry a no-op comparison, r0_m6 rests on 5 'held' rows, and every threshold is the proposer's guess. The FINDINGS itself concedes the range-day idea was never tested.
